metaDescription: Free online Ollama Modelfile generator. Set FROM, PARAMETERs, SYSTEM prompt, TEMPLATE presets, ADAPTER, stop tokens and example messages.
intro: Build an Ollama Modelfile with FROM, PARAMETER values, a SYSTEM prompt, a TEMPLATE preset, an optional ADAPTER, stop tokens and example MESSAGE lines.
why:
Customising a local model with Ollama means writing a Modelfile, and the format has its own rules: triple-quoted SYSTEM and TEMPLATE blocks, one PARAMETER per line and quoted stop tokens. A small mistake means the model silently ignores a setting.

Enter the base model or a .gguf path, tune temperature, context size, top_p, top_k, repeat penalty and other parameters, and write your system prompt. Extra lines let you add stop tokens and example conversation turns. You can choose a template preset such as a Llama 3 chat format, ChatML or Mistral, but it should match the model you start from, because a wrong template degrades answers. Zero values for optional parameters are omitted. Nothing is uploaded.
howTo: Enter the FROM model name or the path to a .gguf file.
Set the parameters you care about, such as temperature and num_ctx; use 0 to leave optional ones out.
Write the system prompt in the first box, and stop tokens or example messages in the second.
Choose a template preset if needed, then copy the Modelfile and run ollama create.

faq.q: How do I add stop tokens or example messages?
faq.a: Use the second box. Write stop: followed by the token for a stop sequence, and user: or assistant: lines for example conversation turns. Each becomes a PARAMETER stop or MESSAGE line.
The one that matches your model. Llama 3, ChatML and Mistral each expect a specific format. If you leave it on none, Ollama uses the template built into the base model, which is usually right.

faq.q: Why are some parameters missing from the output?
faq.a: Optional values such as num_ctx, top_p and top_k are left out when set to 0 so the model default applies. Temperature is always written.

faq.q: Can my system prompt contain triple quotes?
faq.a: No. The SYSTEM block is wrapped in triple quotes, so a prompt containing them would break the file, and the tool shows an error. Rephrase that part.
